Single-cell proteome allocation model for Colonial Trichodesmium#

Temperature response under limiting PO₄, and DOP (PRP)#

This notebook implements the proteome-allocation optimization model for colonial Trichodesmium described in Osorio-Rodriguez et al. (2026, in prep.). The model predicts how a colonial Trichodesmium cell optimally allocates its proteome (the total protein investment across all metabolic functions) to maximize growth rate under a range of temperatures, with phosphorus supplied exclusively as inorganic phosphate (PO₄) and phycosphere-related phosphorus (PRP, here called DOP).

This specific notebook simulates:

  • Organism: colonial Trichodesmium (nitrogen-fixing, filamentous, photosynthetic cyanobacterium)

  • Environmental sweep: temperature range 18–35°C

  • Phosphorus sources: PO₄ = 0.0 µM (absent), DOP = 0.36 µM (dissolved organic phosphorus supplied by the microbiome)

  • DIN: 0.0 µM (nitrogen supplied exclusively by N₂ fixation)

  • Light: 320 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹

Key scientific question: How does warming affect the optimal proteome allocation, growth rate, nitrogen fixation, and phosphorus acquisition strategy of colonial Trichodesmium when phosphorus is supplied as PRP rather than inorganic phosphate?

Model framework: The model uses nonlinear programming (NLP) via JuMP/Ipopt in Julia to find the proteome allocation that maximizes growth rate subject to mass balance, energetic, stoichiometric, and physical constraints. Each enzyme pool is treated as an optimization variable whose concentration is determined by the cell’s optimal investment.

Model Parameters#

All fixed biophysical parameters are defined here. These include:

  • Kinetic parameters (kref, K): maximum turnover rates and half-saturation constants for each enzymatic reaction

  • Physical constraints: membrane transporter surface area, photosystem volume, cell size limits

  • Temperature response parameters: activation energy (Ea), deactivation energy (Ed), reference temperature (Tref), critical high temperature (Td), and Boltzmann constant (R)

  • Stoichiometric parameters: molecular weights of all protein complexes, C:N:P ratios of different cellular components, energy conversion factors (ATP costs per reaction)

The temperature range Ttest (3–45°C, converted to Kelvin) defines the environmental sweep for this notebook.

Load Packages and Initialize the Optimization Model#

Loads the required Julia packages and initializes the JuMP optimization model using Ipopt as the nonlinear solver.

  • JuMP: Julia’s mathematical programming interface. Defines variables, constraints, and objectives

  • Ipopt: Interior Point OPTimizer. The NLP solver used to find the optimal proteome allocation

  • CSV / DataFrames: for storing and exporting model output

  • Plots: for visualization

Environmental parameters are initialized as NLparameters (nonlinear parameters in JuMP), which allows them to be updated between solver calls without rebuilding the full model. This is what makes the environmental sweep in later cells efficient: only the parameter values change, not the model structure.

Initial values here represent standard conditions (T = 26°C, DIN = 1 µM, DIC = 100 µM, PO₄ = 0.1 µM, DOP = 0, I = 320 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹). These are overridden during the environmental sweep.

# Load packages
using Ipopt
using JuMP
using CSV
using DataFrames
using Plots

# Create a JuMP model, using Ipopt as the solver.
model = Model(Ipopt.Optimizer)

# Set the environment:
@NLparameter(model, T   == 26.0 + 273.0)   # K,  temperature
@NLparameter(model, DIN == 1.0)            # uM, external dissolved inorganic nitrogen
@NLparameter(model, DIC == 100.0)          # uM, external dissolved inorganic carbon
@NLparameter(model, PO4 == 0.1)            # uM, external PO4 
@NLparameter(model, DOP == 0.0)            # uM, external DOP
@NLparameter(model, I   == 320.0)          # μmol photon m-2 s-1, irradiance
\[I == 320.0\]

Starting Point (Initial Guess)#

Provides initial values (gs_*) for all optimization variables. The NLP solver requires a feasible starting point; these values correspond to a converged solution at standard conditions.

A good starting point is critical for convergence in nonlinear optimization, particularly for this model, which has many interacting constraints. These values were obtained from a prior solved instance at T = 26°C and represent a biologically reasonable proteome allocation for colonial Trichodesmium.

Define Optimization Variables#

Declares all free variables that the optimizer can adjust to maximize growth rate. These fall into three categories:

Protein concentrations (p*, molecules/µm³): the density of each enzyme complex in the cell (photosystems (pp), ribosomes (pri), rubisco (pru), nitrogenase (pnt), transporters, and metabolic enzymes).

Proteome allocation fractions (ϕ*, dimensionless): the fraction of total protein synthesis flux invested in each enzyme type. These must sum to 0.5 (the other 0.5 being the fraction comprised by proteome not explicitly represented in the model (‘other’)).

Internal metabolite pools (c*, molecules/µm³): concentrations of key intracellular carbon (cic), nitrogen (cin), phosphorus (cip), organic molecules for export (ciorg), membrane lipids (clm), and lipid storage (ctag).

Cell geometry: cell radius (r) and length (h, constrained to 16.2 µm for colonial Trichodesmium based on Cleveland et al. measurements).

Lipid partitioning fractions (αlm, αtag): the fraction of lipid synthesis flux directed toward membrane lipids vs. storage lipids.

# Define the unknown variables that we will optimize for.
@variables(model, begin
        logμ, (start = gs_mu)              # 1/minute, log growth rate 
        pdin ≥ 0, (start = gs_pdin)        # protein: number of DIN proteins without transporters / μm3
        ptrdop ≥ 0, (start = gs_ptrdop)    # protein: number of DOP transporters / μm3
        ptrpo4 ≥ 0, (start = gs_ptrpo4)    # protein: number of PO4 transporters / μm3
        pdop ≥ 0, (start = gs_pdop)        # protein: number of DOP processing proteins / μm3 
        pexp ≥ 0, (start = gs_pexp)        # protein: number of exporters/ μm3 
        porg ≥ 0, (start = gs_porg)        # protein: number of proteins that synthesize organic molecules to export/ μm3 
        ptrn ≥ 0, (start = gs_ptrn)        # protein: number of  transporters / um3
        pnt ≥ 0, (start = gs_pnt)          # protein: number of  nitrogenasse / um3
        pri ≥ 0, (start = gs_pri)          # protein: number of ribosomes / um3 30
        plb ≥ 0, (start = gs_plb)          # protein: number of lipid biosynthesis pathway proteins / um3
        pp  ≥ 0, (start = gs_pp)           # protein: number of photosystems / um3
        pdp ≥ 0, (start = gs_pdp)          # protein: number of damaged photosystems / um3
        pru ≥ 0, (start = gs_pru)          # protein: number of rubisco / um3
        pgl ≥ 0, (start = gs_pgl)          # protein: number of glycolysis pathway prteins / um3
        pre ≥ 0, (start = gs_pre)          # protein: number of repair proteins / um3
        cin ≥ 0, (start = gs_cin)          # other macromolecule: number of internal nitrogen molecules / um3
        cip ≥ 0, (start = gs_cip)          # other macromolecule: number of internal phosphorus atoms / μm3 
        ciorg ≥ 0, (start = gs_ciorg)      # other macromolecule: number of internal organic C and N molecules / μm3

Set Objective Function#

The model maximizes logμ — the log of the instantaneous growth rate (1/minute). Maximizing log growth rate is equivalent to maximizing growth rate and is numerically more stable for the NLP solver.

The solved value is later exponentiated and converted to units of 1/day for biological interpretation.

# Set the objective: maximize the log growth rate (logμ).
@objective(model, Max, logμ)
\[ logμ \]

Define Intermediate Expressions (Reaction Rates and Cell Quantities)#

This cell defines all derived quantities as @NLexpressions: intermediate calculations that depend on the optimization variables and are used in the constraints.

Temperature scaling functions:

  • γTa: Arrhenius scaling for enzyme-catalyzed reactions (activation energy Ea = 4.5 eV)

  • γTd: Arrhenius scaling for heat damage (deactivation energy Ed = 2.0 eV)

  • γTad: Arrhenius scaling for nutrient transport (activation energy Etr = Ea/2 = 2.25 eV)

Reaction rates (v*, molecules/µm³/min): Michaelis-Menten kinetics for each metabolic process (photosynthesis (vp), carbon fixation by rubisco (vru), nitrogen uptake (vtrn), protein synthesis by ribosomes (vri), lipid biosynthesis (vlb), glycolysis (vgl), nitrogen fixation (vnt), PO₄ transport (vtrpo4), DOP processing (vtrdop), export (vexp), and heat damage/repair dynamics (vd, vre)).

Note: DOPt implements a saturating function that scales effective DOP availability with the cell’s export activity (modeling the microbiome interaction where organic molecules excreted by Trichodesmium attract DOP-producing bacteria).

Cell geometry: surface area, volume, surface area-to-volume ratio (β), and free volume fraction (ε) after accounting for photosystems, lipid droplets, nucleoid, and gas vesicles.

Elemental quotas (Qc, Qn, Qp): total carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus per unit biovolume, summing contributions from all protein and macromolecule pools.

# Define any intermediate calculations.
@NLexpressions(model, begin
        #Rate constants
        γTa,   exp(Ea*(1.0/(R*Tref) - 1.0/(R*T)))                                              # rate constant for enzymes; unitless
        γTd,   exp(Ed*(1.0/(R*Td) - 1.0/(R*T)))                                                # rate constant for temperature-dependent damage; unitless
        γTad,  exp(Etr*(1.0/(R*Tref) - 1.0/(R*T)))                                             # rate constant for nitrogen transport; unitless
        γTm,   (Tmax - T)/(Tmax - Tmin)                                                        # unitless
        #Reaction rates 
        vp,  ( kref["p"] ) * pp * I / (K["p"] + I)                                             # photosystems reaction rate; molecules of photons/μm3/min
        vru, ( kref["ru"] * γTa ) * pru * DIC / ( K["ru"] + DIC)                               # rubisco reaction rate; atoms of carbon/μm3/min
        vtrn, ( kref["trn"] * γTad ) * ptrn * DIN/ ( K["trn"] + DIN)                           # DIN reaction rate (limited by the nitrogen transporters reaction rate); atoms of nitrogen/μm3/min
        vri, ( kref["ri"] * γTa ) * pri * (cic / ( K["ic"] + cic )) *                          # Ribosome reaction rate (limited by the nitrogen transporters reaction rate); atoms of nitrogen/μm3/min
        (cin / ( K["in"] + cin))                                                               # protein synthesis rate; molecules of amino acids/μm3/min
        vlb, ( kref["lb"] * γTa ) * plb * cic / ( K["lb"] + cic )                              # lipid synthesis rate; atoms of carbon/μm3/min
        vexp, ( kref["exp"] * γTad) * pexp * (ciorg / (K["exp"] + ciorg))                      # C and N molecules export rate; C and N molecules/μm3/min
        vorg, ( kref["org"] * γTa) * porg * (cic / ( K["corg"] + cic )) *                      # C and N molecules synthesis rate; C and N molecules/μm3/min
         (cin / ( K["norg"] + cin))                                                            
        vgl,   ( kref["gl"] * γTa ) * pgl                                                      # glycolysis rate; atoms of carbon/μm3/min 
        vnt,   ( kref["nt"] * γTa ) * pnt                                                      # N2 fixation rate; atoms of nitrogen/μm3/min  
        DOPt, (vexp  / (vexp+50)) * DOP                                                        # saturating function for DOP in exchange of C and N molecules exported, μM 
        vnt_d,  ( kref["nt_d"]  * γTd ) * pnt * (alpha/r)                                      # rate of nitrogenase damage; molecules of photosystems/μm3/min
        vd,  ( kref["d"]  * γTd ) * pp * (ctag_max/ctag)                                       # rate of heat damage; molecules of photosystems/μm3/min                                                                          
        vre,  ( kref["re"]  * γTa ) * pre * (pdp/(pdp + pp))                                   # rate of repair; molecules of photosystems/μm3/min
        vtrdop, ( kref["trpo4"] * γTad) * ptrpo4 * (DOPt / (K["trpo4"] + DOPt))                # DOP processing rate; molecules of DOP/μm3/min
        vtrpo4, ( kref["trpo4"] * γTad) * ptrpo4 * (PO4 / (K["trpo4"] + PO4))                  # PO4 processing rate; molecules of PO4/μm3/min
        #Cell dimensions
        transporter_sa_vol, 2/r                                                                # SA of only cell lengths: vol, 1/μm
        sa_ends, 2*pi*r^2                                                                      # surface area of ends of cylinder only (without cylinder; μm2)
        sa_l, 2*pi*r*h                                                                         # surface area of cylinder only (without ends; μm2)
        vol, π*r^2*h                                                                           # cell biovolume; μm3
        sa, sa_l + sa_ends                                                                     # cell surface area; μm2
        β, sa/vol                                                                              # surface area: volume of the entire cell; 1/μm
        sa_tr, sa_l/sa                                                                         # cell surface area; μm2
        clm_l, clm* sa_tr                                                                      # molecules of lipid storage/μm3 (required to fuel dark respiration)
        Vn, ((3.14/1.3)* 0.5* 2*h*r) + 0.5                                                     # um3, volume / nucleoid
        ϵ, 1.0 - (pp + pdp) * Vp  - (ctag * Vli) - (Vn/vol) - Vgv                              # fraction of the biovolume not occupied by photosystems nor lipid storage; unitless  

        #Macromolecule pools
        cgu, vgl / ηguc * td                                                                   # storage pool for glucose to fuel dark respiration; molecules of glucose/μm3
        ηaan, ηaac * ((ϕtrn + ϕru + ϕgl + ϕlb + ϕnt + ϕdin + ϕdop                              # atoms of nitrogen / molecule of amino acid
        + ϕexp + ϕorg + ϕtrdop + ϕtrpo4 + ϕre)*Qpt + ϕri*Qri + ϕp*Qp)                                
        tot_p, pp*ηp + pru*ηru + ptrn*ηtrn + pdin*ηdin + pri*ηri + pgl*ηgl +                   # total protein content; Da/μm3
        ptrdop*ηtrdop + ptrpo4*ηtrpo4 + pnt*ηnt + pexp*ηexp + 
        porg*ηorg + plb*ηlb + pre*ηre + cot*ηot                                                          
        ecost, vtrn*(e_trn+e_din) + vri*e_ri +                                                 # energetic demands of photosystems other than rubisco; molecules of ATP/μm3/min
        vtrpo4*e_trpo4 + vexp*e_exp + vorg*e_exp + vlb*e_lb + vd*e_u + vre*e_re                                  
        D, ηru*pru + ηri*pri + ηnt*pnt + pdin*ηdin + ηgl*pgl + pdop*ηdop + ηre*pre             # concentration of all macromolecules except for photosystems, lipid storage and membrane components; Da/μm3 
        + porg*ηorg + plb*ηlb + ηin*cin + ηic*cic + ηip*cip + cgu*ηgu + cot*ηot                             
        #Element concentrations
        atp, (ecost/exp(logμ))*0.001                                                           # total molecules of ATP in the cell/μm3
        Qn,   (ptrn*ηtrn*Qpt + pdin*ηdin*Qpt + pru*ηru*Qpt + pgl*ηgl*Qpt + plb*ηlb*Qpt +       # total number of atoms of nitrogen/μm3
        pri*ηri*Qri + pnt*ηnt*Qpt + ptrdop*ηtrdop*Qpt + ptrpo4*ηtrpo4*Qpt + pdop*ηdop*Qpt + 
        pexp*ηexp*Qpt + porg*ηorg*Qpt + pp*ηp*Qp + pre*ηre*Qpt + cot*ηot*Qpt)* ηaac/ηaa + cin

Linear Constraints#

Defines constraints that are linear and can be handled by the LP layer of the solver:

  • Proteome budget: all proteome allocation fractions (ϕ*) must sum to 0.5, reserving the other 0.5 for housekeeping proteins not explicitly modeled

  • Lipid partitioning: αlm + αtag = 1 (all lipid synthesis flux goes to either membrane lipids or storage)

  • Colonial phenotype-specific constraints: ϕtrdop == 0 and ϕdop == 0 — in this colonial model variant, DOP processing proteins are zeroed out because the microbiome (not the cell itself) is assumed to supply alkaline phosphatase activity.

# Define the system of equations and constraints.
@constraints(model, begin
        ϕp + ϕru + ϕtrn + ϕdin + ϕri + ϕgl + ϕnt + ϕdop + ϕexp + ϕorg + ϕtrdop +               # the sum of all proteome relative investments is assumed to equal 1 - ϕother
        ϕtrpo4 + ϕlb + ϕre ==  0.5 
        αlm + αtag == 1.0                                                                      # the lipids pool is comprised of the flux used to synthesize membrane lipids (αlm), and the storage ones (αtag) 
        # ϕnt ==0 
        ϕtrdop == 0
        ϕdop == 0
end)

(ϕtrn + ϕdin + ϕtrpo4 + ϕdop + ϕtrdop + ϕorg + ϕri + ϕp + ϕru + ϕgl + ϕnt + ϕexp + ϕre + ϕlb = 0.5, αlm + αtag = 1, ϕtrdop = 0, ϕdop = 0)

Nonlinear Constraints#

The core of the model is a system of nonlinear equations and inequalities that enforce biophysical realism:

Protein turnover balance (one equation per protein type): at steady state, the rate of synthesis of each protein (ϕ * vri * 1/(η/ηaa)) must equal the rate of dilution by growth (exp(logμ) * p). This is the fundamental proteome allocation equation: it links proteome investment fractions to absolute protein concentrations.

Internal pool balances (mass balance equations):

  • Nitrogen pool (cin): influx from DIN uptake + N₂ fixation = consumption by protein synthesis + growth dilution

  • Carbon pool (cic): influx from carbon fixation = consumption by ribosomes + lipid synthesis + glycolysis + organic synthesis + growth dilution

  • Phosphorus pool (cip): influx from PO₄ and DOP transport = consumption by membrane phospholipids + ATP + rubisco + glycolysis phosphate groups + growth dilution

  • Organic export pool (ciorg): synthesis rate = export rate + growth dilution

Physical constraints:

  • Membrane composition: transporter-to-lipid ratio within biological bounds (Mmin to Mmax)

  • Cell geometry: surface area equals the sum of transporter and lipid membrane footprints

  • Density: total macromolecular density cannot exceed the biological maximum (Dmax)

  • Free volume fraction (ε): must remain positive after photosystems, lipid droplets, and nucleoid occupy their volumes

Energetic constraints:

  • Photosynthesis must supply enough ATP to run rubisco and nitrogenase

  • Glycolysis must supply enough ATP for dark respiration

  • Total ATP demand from all other processes cannot exceed the surplus from photosynthesis

Heat damage dynamics: damaged photosystem fraction is set by the balance between temperature-dependent damage rate and temperature-dependent repair rate.

@NLconstraints(model, begin
        h == 16.2                                                                             # constraint on the maximum length of cells based on Cleveland et al. measurements
        ϵ ≥ 0
        (ptrn + ptrdop + pexp + ptrpo4) / (clm_l) ≤ Mmax                                      # constraint on the transporter to lipid ratio in the membrane
        vtrn /kref["din"] ≤ pdin                                                              # constraint on the ratio of N transporter to DIN proteins
        # vtrdop /kref["dop"] ≤ pdop                                                            # constraint on the ratio of DOP transporter to processing proteins
        β == (s_trn * (ptrn + ptrdop + pexp + ptrpo4) +                                       # constraint on the volume to surface area ratio of the cell
        s_lm * clm)                                                               
        pdp / (pdp + pp) == ( ( kref["d"]  * γTd ) * pp * (ctag_max/ctag) ) /                 # damage (vd) and repair (vre) dynamics assuming vd = vre
        ( kref["re"] * γTa * pre )                                                             
        ϕp * vri * 1/(ηp/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * (pp) == 0.0                                       # protein: molecules of photosystems/μm3
        ϕru * vri * 1/(ηru/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * pru == 0.0                                      # protein: rubisco/μm3
        ϕtrn  * vri * 1/(ηtrn/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * ptrn  == 0.0                                 # protein: N transporters/μm3
        ϕdin  * vri * 1/(ηdin/ηaa)  - exp(logμ) * pdin  == 0.0                                # protein: DIN proteins/μm3
        ϕri * vri * 1/(ηri/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * pri == 0.0                                      # protein: ribosomes/μm3
        ϕnt * vri * 1/(ηnt/ηaa)  - vnt_d- exp(logμ) * pnt == 0.0                              # protein: nitrogenase/μm3
        ϕlb * vri * 1/(ηlb/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * plb == 0.0                                      # protein: lipid synthesis proteins/μm3
        ϕgl * vri * 1/(ηgl/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * pgl == 0.0                                      # protein: glycolysis proteins/μm3
        ϕre * vri * 1/(ηre/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * pre == 0.0                                      # protein: pre/μm3
        ϕtrpo4 * vri * 1/(ηtrpo4/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * ptrpo4 == 0.0                             # protein: PO4 transporters/μm3
        ϕdop * vri * 1/(ηdop/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * pdop == 0.0                                   # protein: DOP processing proteins/μm3
        ϕtrdop * vri * 1/(ηtrdop/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * ptrdop == 0.0                             # protein: DOP transporters/μm3
        ϕexp * vri * 1/(ηexp/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * pexp == 0.0                                   # protein: exporters/μm3
        ϕorg * vri * 1/(ηorg/ηaa) - exp(logμ) * porg == 0.0                                   # protein: synthesis of molecules to export/μm3
        vtrn + vnt - vri*ηaan - vorg - exp(logμ) * cin == 0.0                                 # internal pool of nitrogen/μm3
        vru - vri*ηaac - vlb - vgl - vorg*3 - exp(logμ) * cic == 0.0                          # internal pool of carbon/μm3
        vtrpo4 + vtrdop  - vgl*ec_gl*ηatpp/ηguc - vri*ϕru*ηrup*ηaa/(ηaac*ηru) -               # internal pool of phosphorus/μm3
        exp(logμ)*clm*flmp*ηlip - exp(logμ) * cip == 0.0                           
        vorg - vexp -  exp(logμ) * ciorg == 0.0                                               # internal pool of N and C molecules to export/μm3
        αlm * vlb/ηlic - exp(logμ) * clm == 0.0                                               # membrane lipids/μm3 (evolved)
        αtag * vlb/ηlic - exp(logμ) * ctag == 0.0                                             # lipid storage/μm3 (used to regulate heat-damage; not used in dark respiration)
        ctag ≤ ctag_min + ctag_max                                                            # constraint on the maximum concentration of ctag; lipid storage/μm3
        # energetic requirements:
        vp * e_p ≥ vru * e_ru + vnt * e_nt                                                    # rubisco costs are paid by photosystems; molecules of ATP/μm3/min
        ecost ≤ vp * e_p - vru * e_ru - vnt * e_nt                                            # total ATP cost; molecules of ATP/μm3/min
        ecost*fdr ≤ vgl * ep_gl                                                               # dark respiration; molecules of ATP/μm3/min
        1/ϵ * D ≤ Dmax                                                                        # density constraint; Da/μm3  
end)

Initial Solve#

Solves the optimization problem once at the initial parameter values (T = 26°C). This confirms the model is feasible and the starting point is valid before beginning the environmental sweep. The status variable should return LOCALLY_SOLVED.

# Solve the optimization problem.
status = optimize!(model)

Define Environmental Sweep#

Sets up the parameter ranges for the environmental sweep. For this notebook (env == "Temperature (C°)"):

  • Temperature: 18–35°C in 0.05°C steps (341 values)

  • DIN: 0.0 µM — nitrogen supplied only by N₂ fixation

  • Light: 320 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ (fixed)

  • DOP: 0.36 µM — phosphonate-rich particles supplied by the colonial microbiome

  • PO₄: 0.0 µM — no inorganic phosphate

This configuration isolates the temperature response of colonial Trichodesmium under phosphorus limitation from inorganic sources, with the microbiome providing DOP as the sole phosphorus source. This is the ecologically relevant condition for oligotrophic open-ocean environments where inorganic phosphate concentrations are often below detection limits.

# Optimal solutions looping over different environmental conditions.
env = "Temperature (C°)" # should be one of the following: [DIN], Temperature (C°), "Light", "[DOP]", "[PO4]"

if env == "[DIN]"
    # Run varying [DIN].
    change_DIN = 10.0 .^ [-7.0:0.18:log10(20.0);]
    change_T = 26.0 + 273.0
    change_I = 320.0
    change_DOP = 0.0
    change_PO4 = 0.5
elseif env == "Temperature (C°)"
    # Run varying Temperature.
    change_DIN = 0.0
    change_T  = 273.0 .+ [18:0.05:35.0;]
    change_I = 320.0
    change_DOP = 0.36
    change_PO4 = 0.0
elseif env == "Light"
    # Run varying Light.
    change_DIN = 0.0
    change_T = 26.0 + 273.0
    change_I = 10.0 .^ [-7.0:0.18:log10(120.0);]
    change_DOP = 0.0
    change_PO4 = 5.0
elseif env == "[DOP]"
    # Run varying DOP.
    change_DIN = 1.0
    change_T = 26.0 + 273.0
    change_I = 320.0
    change_DOP = 10.0 .^ [-1.0:0.1:log10(10.0);]
    change_PO4 = 0.0
elseif env == "[PO4]"
    # Run varying PO4.
    change_DIN = 1.0
    change_T = 26.0 + 273.0
    change_I = 320.0
    change_DOP = 0.0
    change_PO4 = 10.0 .^ [-3.0:0.1:log10(3.2);]
end

Pre-allocate Output Arrays#

Pre-allocates 5-dimensional arrays for all output variables. The five dimensions correspond to the five environmental axes: temperature (change_T), DIN (change_DIN), light (change_I), DOP (change_DOP), and PO₄ (change_PO4). For this notebook, four of the five dimensions have length 1 (scalar fixed conditions), so the arrays are effectively 1D sweeps over temperature.

Variables stored include all protein concentrations (s_p*), proteome fractions (s_ϕ*), internal pools (s_c*), reaction rates (s_v*), elemental quotas (s_Q*), cell geometry, temperature scaling factors, and environmental parameter values.

Run the Environmental Sweep#

The main computation loop. For each combination of environmental conditions, updates the NLparameters and re-solves the optimization problem, then stores all output variables in the pre-allocated arrays.

The nested loop structure (DIN → Temperature → Light → DOP → PO₄) follows the pre-allocated array indexing. Because most dimensions are scalar for this notebook, only the temperature loop is active.

The solver re-uses the previous solution as a warm start for the next temperature step, which improves convergence speed and solution continuity. Solutions that fail to converge are stored as whatever the solver returns at termination (these are filtered out in a later cell based on biological plausibility criteria).

# Store model output in empty vectors
for i in 1:length(change_DIN)
    set_value(DIN, change_DIN[i])
    for j in 1:length(change_T)
            set_value(T, change_T[j])

Flatten Output Arrays#

Reshapes the 5-dimensional output arrays into 1-dimensional vectors for DataFrame construction. The total number of rows equals the product of all environmental sweep lengths.

The variable names here map to biological quantities:

  • mu: growth rate (1/day, converted from 1/min)

  • NC: C:N ratio of the cell

  • Pcell: C:P ratio of the cell

  • init: proteome fraction in nitrogenase (N₂ fixation)

  • itrpo4: proteome fraction in PO₄ transporters

  • vnt: N₂ fixation rate (atoms N/µm³/min)

  • vtrpo4: PO₄ transport rate

  • vtrdop: DOP processing rate (here zeroed out for the colonial model)

  • ctag: storage lipid concentration (lipid droplets/µm³)

# Reshape the array into a 1-dimensional array
temp = reshape(s_T .- 273.0, (a * b * c * d * e , 1))
volume = reshape(s_vol, (a * b * c * d * e , 1))

using CSV using DataFrames

a = length(change_T) b = length(change_DIN) c = length(change_I) d = length(change_DOP) e = length(change_PO4)

Flatten Output Arrays#

Reshapes the 5-dimensional output arrays into 1-dimensional vectors for DataFrame construction. The total number of rows equals the product of all environmental sweep lengths.

The variable names here map to biological quantities:

  • mu: growth rate (1/day, converted from 1/min)

  • NC: C:N ratio of the cell

  • Pcell: C:P ratio of the cell

  • init: proteome fraction in nitrogenase (N₂ fixation)

  • itrpo4: proteome fraction in PO₄ transporters

  • vnt: N₂ fixation rate (atoms N/µm³/min)

  • vtrpo4: PO₄ transport rate

  • vtrdop: DOP processing rate (here zeroed out for the colonial model)

  • ctag: storage lipid concentration (lipid droplets/µm³)

Export to CSV (Optional)#

Exports the full output DataFrame to model_output.csv. This line is commented out by default — uncomment to save results for external analysis or to reproduce figures without re-running the solver.

# CSV.write("model_output.csv", output, header = true)

Convert Temperature Units#

Converts change_T from Kelvin to Celsius for plotting. This is done after the solver loop because the solver requires Kelvin internally but figures use Celsius for readability.

# Convert temperature to degree Celsius
change_T = change_T .- 273.0

Filter Solutions#

Removes solver outputs that are biologically implausible or numerically problematic:

  • eps < 0.1: excludes solutions where the free volume fraction (ε) is too large, indicating the cell interior is nearly empty — a sign of a degenerate solution

  • eps > -0.00001: excludes solutions where free volume is slightly negative (numerical artifact)

  • mu > 0.01 and mu < 0.5: keeps only solutions in the biologically realistic growth rate range for Trichodesmium (roughly 0.01–0.5 divisions/day)

The filtered DataFrame filtered_df is used for all subsequent visualization.

# Set threshold
up_threshold = 0.1
sec_up_threshold = 0.001
low_threshold= -0.00001

# Filter rows where score > up_threshold or < low_threshold
filtered_df = output[output.eps .< up_threshold, :]
# filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df.eps .> sec_up_threshold, :]
filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df.eps .> low_threshold, :]
filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df.mu .> 0.01, :]
filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df.mu .< 0.5, :]


# filtered_df = filtered_df[Not([52,53]),:]

# filtered_df = output

Visualization#

Generates a 4×4 panel plot showing key model outputs as functions of temperature (18–35°C). Each panel shows a different physiological or biochemical variable:

Panel layout:

  1. Exporter concentration (pexp) vs. temperature

  2. Transporter surface-to-volume ratio and total SA:V ratio vs. temperature

  3. Main proteome allocation fractions: photosystems, glycolysis, rubisco, ribosomes, nitrogenase, PO₄ transport

  4. N₂ fixation and DIN uptake rates (log scale)

  5. Cell radius vs. temperature

  6. Growth rate (1/day) vs. temperature

  7. Absolute concentrations of photosystems, glycolysis, rubisco, ribosomes (molecules/µm³)

  8. (Commented out: elemental quotas and ratios)

  9. Export allocation fraction vs. temperature

  10. PO₄ transport allocation fraction vs. temperature

  11. DOP and PO₄ processing rates vs. temperature

  12. Photosystem and rubisco reaction rates vs. temperature

  13. Export rate vs. temperature

  14. Nitrogenase, DIN reduction, and DIN transporter concentrations vs. temperature

  15. N₂ fixation and DIN uptake rates normalized by ATP cost (metabolic efficiency)

  16. Storage lipid concentration (ctag) vs. temperature

The figure is saved to PDF when the savefig line is uncommented. The commented-out panels show alternative analyses explored during model development.

using Plots
using Printf
gr()

tic1 = 10.0 .^ collect(range(1,10,step=1))
plot(layout = (4,4), guidefontsize = 9)
